decisions.title: Three-layer spacing token system adopted
decisions.decision: Spacing tokens follow three layers: primitive (raw values), semantic (layout rules), and component (platform-specific exceptions). This mirrors the pattern already used for colors and typography.
decisions.rationale: A three-layer system allows combining and nesting design modes (platform, brand, accessibility) without creating an explosion of top-level tokens. The semantic layer keeps design decisions consistent; the component layer isolates exceptions so the semantic layer stays clean.
constraints: Semantic layer must remain finite — it should not 'explode'
Component layer is reserved for platform-specific exceptions only, not general component styling
Follows the same pattern as colors and typography

decisions.title: Token layer terminology standardised
decisions.decision: Agreed terminology across all platforms: 'reference' = primitive layer, 'system' = semantic layer, 'component' = component layer.
decisions.rationale: Different participants were using 'semantic' and 'system' interchangeably. Aligning on one vocabulary prevents confusion in cross-platform discussions.

decisions.title: 4-point spacing grid adopted
decisions.decision: Spacing primitives are based on a 4-point grid, not 8-point.
decisions.rationale: Provides finer granularity needed for micro-spacing decisions while still maintaining a systematic scale.

decisions.title: Semantic layer governance: automated, finite, all-platform approval required
decisions.decision: Any changes to primitive or semantic layer tokens must be agreed upon by all platforms (iOS, Android, web). The semantic layer must be automated and kept finite. Changes will flow through a dedicated Slack channel or MR approval process.
decisions.rationale: The semantic layer acts as a shared contract. Unilateral changes create blast-radius problems across all platforms. Automation ensures consistency and prevents manual drift.
constraints: No token additions to primitive or semantic layers without cross-platform sign-off
Automation is a prerequisite for the semantic layer to be viable at scale

decisions.title: Component layer restricted to platform-specific exceptions
decisions.decision: Component-level spacing tokens are allowed but must be reserved for genuine platform-specific differences (e.g. iOS vs Android measurement conventions, accessibility safe-area insets). They are not to be created for general component styling.
decisions.rationale: Rasmus' experience at a previous company showed that full component tokenisation resulted in enormous overhead (10,000+ tokens) with only 0.5% of them ever deviating from the default. Patrick emphasised that component token explosion would hurt code scalability.
constraints: Only introduce a component token when the semantic layer cannot handle the exception
Component tokens must be agreed before creation, not added ad-hoc

decisions.title: Semantic spacing layer: four use cases defined
decisions.decision: The semantic spacing layer has four named use cases: edge (space from a container's outermost boundary to its first child), flow (vertical space between elements), inline (horizontal space between elements), gutter (outermost page-level space, replacing the term 'boundary').
decisions.rationale: Provides a finite, meaningful vocabulary for spacing decisions that works across platforms. 'Gutter' was accepted over 'boundary' as clearer terminology. 'Flow' was accepted for vertical spacing despite Android naming conflicts because perfect naming was unattainable and progress needed to be made.
constraints: edge: from container edge to first child element
flow: vertical gap between elements (e.g. items in a list)
inline: horizontal gap between elements (e.g. icon and text in a button)
gutter: outermost space from page edge to first layout element — used at page level only

decisions.title: No platform-specific values in the primitive layer
decisions.decision: iOS-specific primitives (e.g. safe area insets) must not be added to the primitive layer. Platform differences are handled via Figma modes at the semantic or component layer.
decisions.rationale: Adding iOS-specific primitives would pollute the shared primitive set. Figma modes already provide the mechanism to deliver different values per platform from the same token name.

decisions.title: Size tokens are distinct from spacing tokens
decisions.decision: Size tokens (stroke width, font size, icon size, etc.) are a separate primitive category from spacing tokens. The two must not be mixed.
decisions.rationale: Spacing describes the distance between or around elements. Size describes the dimensions of elements themselves. Conflating them leads to misuse and token bloat.

decisions.title: Primitive set must be minimal and justified; new values increment by 4
decisions.decision: The primitive spacing set starts as small as possible. Values are only added when a concrete use case is demonstrated (e.g. via scaled-up page examples). Any new value added must be a multiple of 4. Large values like 128 must be explicitly justified before inclusion.
decisions.rationale: Starting large creates values that will be misused as shortcuts instead of correctly implementing constraints. The process for adding new primitives (with justification) prevents bloat and preserves the integrity of the system.
constraints: All primitives must be multiples of 4
A use case must be demonstrated before a new primitive is added
Large values (>80) require explicit written justification

decisions.title: Layer responsibility: semantic = brand, component = platform
decisions.decision: The semantic layer handles brand-level differences (e.g. Boost vs Outlet Nation spacing). The component layer handles platform-level differences (e.g. iOS 44dp vs Android 48dp touch targets on buttons).
decisions.rationale: Clarifies the distinct purpose of each layer and prevents the two concerns from bleeding into each other. Brand modes in Figma operate at the semantic layer (same mechanism as colors); platform specifics require component-level tokens to be isolated.

decisions.title: Primitives must not be exposed to developers in code
decisions.decision: The token export script must be updated so that only semantic layer tokens (edge, flow, inline, gutter with their size variants) are accessible to developers. Primitive tokens must not be directly reachable in code.
decisions.rationale: The current script exports everything indiscriminately. If primitives are accessible, developers will use them directly instead of going through the semantic layer, bypassing the system's intent and making future changes unsafe.
constraints: Export script must filter to semantic layer and above only
This is a prerequisite before the spacing system can be considered production-ready
